record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How can heavy-ion collision models consistently describe the photon and dilepton consequences of hard-parton energy loss, including additional jet-medium photons and dileptons produced by the energy-loss processes and the simultaneous suppression or modification of fragmentation photons, when the problem combines the space-time dependence of parton energy loss with low-energy parton and photon production?

evidence.quote: We use “(parton energy loss)” as a short-hand for the complex energy loss process through which hard partons interact with the lower-energy bath of quarks and gluons.

This combination of the momentum-space formulation of Eq. 6 with the space-time dependence of parton energy loss is a significant challenge of Eq. 7; in practice, Eq. 7 is generally solved with Monte Carlo event generators.

For photons (and dileptons), the “(parton energy loss)” part of Eq. 7 already has one consequence: the processes that lead to parton energy loss will also produce additional photons and dileptons, known as “jet-medium photons and dileptons”.

Overall, the combination of additional jet-medium radiation and suppressed fragmentation photons remains a remarkably difficult phenomenon to model, combining all the challenges of parton energy loss with that of low-energy parton and photon production.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the theoretical description of relativistic heavy-ion collisions, hard partons produced in initial hard scatterings traverse a hot and dense medium of quarks and gluons (the quark-gluon plasma) and lose energy through interactions with this lower-energy thermal bath. Schematically, the inclusive yield of a particle species X (X = hadron, photon, or lepton pair) takes the form of a convolution

    dN_X = (initial hard production) ⊗ (parton energy loss) ⊗ (fragmentation / hadronization or photon/dilepton emission),

where the energy-loss kernel must be evolved along the space-time trajectory of each hard parton through a hydrodynamically evolving medium, while the hard production and fragmentation pieces are most naturally formulated in momentum space.

For electromagnetic probes (real photons and dileptons), the energy-loss stage itself emits radiation: bremsstrahlung and medium-induced conversion processes produce so-called jet-medium photons and dileptons, and at the same time the fragmentation contribution to photon (and dilepton) production from the hard parton is suppressed or modified because the parton's momentum and color state have been altered by its passage through the medium.

Problem. Construct a single, theoretically consistent framework — for instance a Monte Carlo or transport scheme — that:

(i) implements parton energy loss as a space-time–dependent process along realistic medium evolution histories,
(ii) simultaneously generates the jet-medium photons and dileptons emitted during the energy-loss process,
(iii) yields the appropriately suppressed/modified fragmentation photon (and dilepton) spectra from the surviving hard partons,
(iv) preserves energy-momentum conservation, color coherence (LPM-type interference) and the correct interface with low-energy (thermal) parton and photon/dilepton production,

and quantitatively reproduces measured nuclear modification factors and direct-photon / dilepton spectra in heavy-ion collisions. Provide the formalism, demonstrate its internal consistency, and compare its predictions with data.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a phenomenological modeling challenge in heavy-ion physics rather than a precisely formulated mathematical conjecture. Recent reviews and modeling efforts (JETSCAPE framework, MARTINI, hybrid strong/weak coupling models) make progress on coupling parton energy loss with electromagnetic radiation, but a fully consistent description that simultaneously captures jet-medium photons/dileptons and modified fragmentation photons across collision systems remains an open modeling problem.

status_evidence.claim: The consistent modeling of jet-medium photons together with modified fragmentation photons is identified as an open challenge.
